test_title: PYST 22 - SSC CHSL 2025 - English Language (Held On: 20 Nov, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: english
question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct voice.**

The student said that the teacher had explained the lesson clearly.

options.text: The student said, "The teacher explained the lesson clearly."
The student said, "The teacher has explained the lesson clearly."
The student said, "The teacher had explained the lesson clearly."
The student said, "The teacher explains the lesson clearly, "

solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. The student said, "The teacher has explained the lesson clearly." .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in **indirect speech**, and the task is to convert it into **direct speech**.
 
• In indirect speech, the past perfect tense (**had explained**) turns into present perfect tense (**has explained**) when converted to direct speech.
 
• The correct option is **Option 2:** The student said, "The teacher has explained the lesson clearly."

Correct sentence: *The student said, "The teacher has explained the lesson clearly."*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rules for converting indirect to direct speech:**

 
 
• In the **past perfect tense**, the verb remains unchanged in direct speech.
 
• Quotation marks (**" "**) are used to enclose the statement.
 
• Ensure the reporting verb (**said**) is followed by a comma before the quoted speech.
 
 
 
• **Other options explained:**
 
 
• **Option 1:** Incorrect because it uses the simple past tense (*explained*), which changes the tense.
 
• **Option 3:** Incorrect because it uses the past perfect tense (*had explained*), which is inconsistent with the original tense.
 
• **Option 4:** Incorrect because it uses the simple present tense (*explains*), which is inconsistent with the original tense.
